subject: Renewal QBR: compressed agenda + calendar trade proposal
messages:
From: Sophia Khan <sophia.khan@cloudvista.com>
To: markus.klein@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@cloudvista.com>
Date: 2026-07-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: compressing our Renewal QBR into 90 minutes — exec availability squeeze

Hi Markus,

Quick ask: our exec sponsor just told us they can only join a 90-minute window on July 28. We know your standard QBR is 2.5 hours with a roadmap demo; is there room to compress to 90 minutes and still cover renewal + high-level roadmap? If so, we need a slimmed agenda and a firm run-of-show so we can lock the C-suite calendar.

Two constraints from our side:
- please keep technical deep-dive to zero — ops leader will take follow-ups offline
- delivery team (Aaron + two engineers) will only attend the demo portion (last 30 min)

Can you propose a compact agenda and confirm who should present each section? Happy to take a trade (e.g., pre-record a 10-min technical clip) if that helps.

Thanks,
Sophia
Sophia Khan
Head of Product, CloudVista
Sophia.Khan@cloudvista.com

Attachments: none
From: markus.klein@redwoodinference.com
To: Sophia Khan <sophia.khan@cloudvista.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, priyom.das@redwoodinference.com, Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@cloudvista.com>
Date: 2026-07-21T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: compressing our Renewal QBR into 90 minutes — exec availability squeeze

Sophia — thanks for the heads up. We can do a compact QBR that preserves renewal decisioning and a focused roadmap demo. Proposed tradeoffs and structure below.

High-level compressed agenda (90 minutes):
- 0–10m: Executive hello + commitment (you + our CRO)
- 10–25m: Renewal summary — usage, cost trends, impact highlights (Ben)
- 25–40m: Customer success highlights + outstanding items (Laura)
- 40–65m: Focused roadmap demo (top 3 features that move the needle) — 15m product, 10m live demo, 5m customer scenarios (Markus + Prio)
- 65–85m: Contract & procurement blockers (if any) + ask for decision next steps (Ben + Prio)
- 85–90m: Close & immediate next step (confirm follow-up owners)

Notes/trade options:
- We can pre-record a 10-min engineering vignette to replace a deep-dive; will attach as a link.
- If the exec wants single-slide technical assurance, we can include a one-slide security/compliance summary in the Renewal summary segment.
- We will keep the demo to no more than 20 minutes (live + scenarios), and Ben will scope the revenue/procurement ask up front so the exec can sign off quickly.

I attached a compact agenda draft and a run-of-show worksheet for you to review. If that works, Laura can send a calendar invite with a hard lock on the 90-min window and speaker assignments.

Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: compact-qbr-agenda-v1.pdf; run_of_show-compact.xlsx

- I'll lead the renewal summary and have a 1-slide economic ask ready (current committed capacity + proposed renewal term).
- Can you confirm who will own procurement pre-reads? If CloudVista can sign a short pre-approval (email) it speeds decisioning.

Operational note: if we keep the live demo to 15 minutes, Aaron’s engineers should be on mute for the earlier parts and join turnaround Q&A for the last 15. Laura — can you own the invite and recording permissions?

Ben
